newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar trims losses from Thai woes by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar trims losses from Thai woes by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0632 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar trimmed its earlier losses against the yen on short-covering by late Tokyo on Wednesday after earlier falling in reaction to an announcement by the Bank of Thailand (BOT) that the Thai baht will be floated, dealers said.
The Thai news initially led to buying of the yen as a safe haven, but most dealers said the impact may be short-lived.
Dealers said the BOT's surprising decision provoked speculation that the Japanese currency could benefit from flight-to-quality buying from South Asian currencies.
U.S. operators, probably operating out of Singapore, were said to be major sellers of dollars for yen following the news, pressuring other traders to unwind their dollar long postions.

But short-covering pushed the greenback back up in afternoon trade after the dollar's downside was tested solid near 114.20 yen. "Some say the yen will be bought as a safe-haven currency after the Thai news, but the impact from it on dollar/yen trade will be limited," a trust bank dealer said.
Afternoon trade was stuck in narrow range, with trade sandwiched by bids from Japanese institutional investors near 114.20 yen and exporter offers near 115 yen, dealers said.

A senior trader at a Japanese bank said BOT's decision is a 'de facto' devaluation of its currency, adding that it suggests more burden on the country in its repayment of external debts. Thailand held a massive 12.935 trillion yen in yen-denominated loans from the Japanese government as of the end of March 1996.
Although the baht nosedived against the dollar following the BOT's announcement, Tokyo dealers said it will take time to digest the news and find an appropriate level for dollar/baht.
"But the BOT said it would intervene, so excessive moves may be limited," said Ken Kawai, manager of the foreign exchange and treasury division, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said that BOT will intervene in foreign exchange markets from time to time to achieve policy objectives and guard against excessive baht fluctuations.

A senior official of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) told Reuters that the flotation of the Thai baht increases the scope for cooperation among central banks and that the Japanese central bank was informed of the news, but was not asked for help.
Some dealers said Japanese investment trust firms which manage baht-related financial instruments may become major sellers of the baht, but others said there has been no panic sales so far.
A city bank dealer said Tokyo players were sidelined as uncertainty remains over details of "a manged float" exchange rate system.
In the offshore market, the Thai baht stood at 28.400/900 to the dollar at 0727 GMT, compared with around 24.25 just before the news.
Dealers in Singapore said they expected the dollar to test the upside of 30.0 baht to one dollar later on Wednesday.

"The market is just looking to find an excuse to sell dollar/yen which has been very firm. It is now in a consolidation phase and I expect it to trade within 113.00/115.50 barring major news," a dealer with a European bank in Singapore said.
Activity of dollar/mark was muted in sidelined trade.
The dollar was at 114.90/95 yen and 1.7468/73 marks in late New York on Tuesday. -- Singapore newsroom +65-8703080
-- Yoko Nishikawa, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8584
